scope: Written invariance/endpoint audit of the existing harmonic criterion, not a new state-family result or independent review.
nondegenerate_axes: For 0<s<1, the actual pure-state polygon gives p_i<=s/2<1/2. Thus each local majority/minority eigenvector is unique up to its own phase, including p_i=0. Changing those four local phases changes the state-coordinate phases but leaves every P_x, every a_x, q4, and W exactly unchanged. Global input phase also cancels. Permuting sites permutes the summands and preserves s, q4 and W. Therefore the criterion is an intrinsic property of the actual state, not a basis-choice-dependent or independent-marginal relaxation.
endpoint_axes: At s>=1 local ties p_i=1/2 may make axes nonunique, but 121 does not use W: H1(sigma)-I is PSD in every diagonalizing local basis, and a single rank-one subtraction has at most one negative eigenvalue. At s=0 all four p_i vanish and a pure sigma is necessarily a product; full spin flip maps it to a pure product rho. The fixed-Q output comparison is an inequality, not automatic equality, as corrected in 127.
spinflip_local_covariance: For any local U(2) matrix U, Y conjugate(U)=det(U)^(-1) U Y. Tensoring over four sites changes a full-spin-flipped vector only by an overall phase, so local rotations commute with spin flip at the density/projector level. No local partial transpose is introduced. Full spin flip preserves local marginal eigenvalues and maps each sigma local majority/minority eigenspace to the complementary rho local eigenspace.
boundary_limit: The eigenvalue criterion itself is continuous as a matrix property, but the coordinate expression W may jump at a zero denominator. The actual physical example and the conditional zero-direction inertia qualification are 140 and 144; do not replace 121's direct pseudoinverse boundary with unproved W continuity.
process: 125,127,128,130,133 remain distinct mandatory source corrections; 132 and 143 remain distinct owner cadence findings. 121/123 remain unreviewed; parent controls source order, classification and any actual reviewer exposure.
